Marginally acceptable hearts can still be used for transplantation, but an important factor to consider is the assessment of left ventricular function using transesophageal echocardiography (TEE). In brain-dead donors, TEE can provide valuable information on the heart's function.

A study found that approximately 36% of potential heart donors have a Failure of Achievement Criteria (FAC) less than 50%, which is considered "marginal acceptable." This means that while not all hearts may meet this threshold for transplantation, many still have sufficient function to be suitable for implantation.
